text:
If a reaction follows the Arrhenius equation, the plot ln k vs $\frac{1}{(RT)}$ gives straight line with a gradient ($-$ y) unit. 

The energy required to active the reactant is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to Arrhenius equation,

k = A$e^{-\frac{Ea}{RT}}$

or ln k = ln A - $\frac{E_{a}}{RT}$

Comparing the above equation
with straight line equation,

y = mx + c,

we get, slope or gradient $(m) = –E_{a}$

and Intercept (c) = ln A

Also given that slope or gradient (m) = -y

$\therefore$ $-y = –E_{a}$

$\Rightarrow$ $E_{a} = y$

So the activation energy of the reactant, $E_{a} = y$ unit
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot

text:
Match the metals (column I) with the coordination compound(s)/enzyme(s) (column II) 

  
    (Column I) Metals

    (Column II) Coordination 
compounds(s) enzyme(s)

  
  
    (A)
    Co
    (i)
    Wilkinson catalyst
  
  
    (B)
    Zn
    (ii)
    Chlorophyl
  
  
    (C)
    Rh
    (iii)
    Vitamin $B_{12}$
  
  
    (D)
    Mg
    (iv)
    Carbonic anhydrase
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Vitamin $\mathrm{B}{}_{12}$ (cyanocobalamin) is a cobalt complex, so Co matches (iii).

Carbonic anhydrase is a zinc enzyme with $\mathrm{Zn}{}^{2+}$ at its active site, so Zn matches (iv).

Wilkinson's catalyst is $[\mathrm{RhCl}(\mathrm{PPh}{}_{3}){}_{3}]$, so Rh matches (i).

Chlorophyll is a porphyrin complex of $\mathrm{Mg}{}^{2+}$, so Mg matches (ii).

The matching is (A)-(iii), (B)-(iv), (C)-(i), (D)-(ii).

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot

text:
For the cell $Zn(s) |Zn^{2+} (aq)| |M^{x+} (aq)| M(s)$, different half cells and their standard electrode potentials are given below : 

  
    $M^{x+} (aq)/M(s)$
    $Au^{3+}(aq)/Au(s)$
    $Ag^{+}(aq)/Ag(s)$
    $Fe^{3+}(aq)/Fe^{2+} (aq)$
    $Fe^{2+}(aq)/Fe(s)$
  
  
    $E^{0}_{M^{x+}}_{/M}/(V)$
    1.40
    0.80
    0.77
    $-$0.44
  

If  $E_{zn^{2+}/zn}^{0}$ = $-$ 0.76 V, which cathode will give maximum value of $E^{o}_{$cell} per electron transferred?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$Zn(s) |Zn^{2+} (aq)| |M^{x+} (aq)| M(s)$

---------------------------------------

        Anode              Cathode

 $E^{o}_{$cell$} = E^{o}_{$cathode$} – E^{o}_{$anode}

(i) For $Ag^{+}/Ag$ :

$E^{o}_{$cell} = 0.80 – (– 0.76) = 1.56 V

No of electrons transferred = LCM of valency factor of two electrode

Valency factor of $Zn(s) |Zn^{2+} = 2$

Valency factor of $Ag^{+}/Ag = 1$

LCM of 1 and 2 = 2

$\therefore$ No of electrons transferred = 2

$\therefore$ $E^{o}_{$cell} per electron = $\frac{1.56}{2}$ = 0.78

(ii) For $Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}$ :

$E^{o}_{$cell} = 0.77 – (– 0.76) = 1.53 V

No of electrons transferred = LCM of valency factor of two electrode

Valency factor of $Zn(s) |Zn^{2+} = 2$

Valency factor of $Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+} = 1$

LCM of 2 and 1 = 2

$\therefore$ No of electrons transferred = 2

$\therefore$ $E^{o}_{$cell} per electron = $\frac{1.53}{2}$ = 0.76

(iii) For $Au^{3+}/Au$ :

$E^{o}_{$cell} = 1.40 – (– 0.76) = 2.16 V

No of electrons transferred = LCM of valency factor of two electrode

Valency factor of $Zn(s) |Zn^{2+} = 2$

Valency factor of $Au^{3+}/Au = 3$

LCM of 2 and 3 = 6

$\therefore$ No of electrons transferred = 6

$\therefore$ $E^{o}_{$cell} per electron = $\frac{2.16}{6}$ = 0.36

(iv) For $Fe^{2+}/Fe$ :

$E^{o}_{$cell} = –0.44 – (– 0.76) = 0.32 V

No of electrons transferred = LCM of valency factor of two electrode

Valency factor of $Zn(s) |Zn^{2+} = 2$

Valency factor of $Fe^{2+}/Fe = 2$

LCM of 2 and 2 = 2

$\therefore$ No of electrons transferred = 2

$\therefore$ $E^{o}_{$cell} per electron = $\frac{0.32}{2}$ = 0.16

$E^{o}_{$cell} is maximum for $E^{o}_{Ag^{+}(aq)/Ag(s)}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot

text:
A 10 mg effervescent tablet containing sodium bicarbonate and oxalic acid releases 0.25 ml of $CO_{2}$ at T = 298.15 K and p = 1 bar. If molar volume of $CO_{2}$ is 25.0 L under such condition, what is the percentage of sodium bicarbonate in each tablet ? 

[Molar mass of NaHCO$_{3} = 84 g$ mol$^{–1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
2NaHCO$_{3}$
 + (COOH$)_{2}$ $\to$ (COONa$)_{2} + 2H_{2}O + 2CO_{2}$

$\therefore$ 1 mole of $CO_{2}$ is produced by 1 mole of NaHCO$_{3}$.

Given, volume of $CO_{2}$ produced = 0.25 ml

25 L of $CO_{2}$ contains 1 mol

$\therefore$ 0.25 ml of $CO_{2}$ contains = $\frac{1}{25\times 10^{3}}\times 0.25$ moles

$= 10^{-5}$ moles

$\therefore$ Moles of NaHCO$_{3} = 10^{-5}$ moles

Mass of NaHCO$_{3} = 10^{-5}$ $\times$ 84 g

$\therefore$ % of NaHCO$_{3}$ in a tablet 

= $\frac{84\times 10^{-5}}{10\times 10^{-3}}\times 100$ = 8.4 %
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot

text:
Consider the reaction 

$N_{2}(g) + 3H_{2}(g)$ $⇌$ $2NH_{3}(g)$

The equilibrium constant of the above reaction is $K_{p}$. If pure ammonia is left to dissociate, the partial pressure of ammonia at equilibrium is given by (Assume that $P_{NH3}  << P_{$total} at equilibrium)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$N_{2}(g) + 3H_{2}(g)$ $⇌$ $2NH_{3}(g)$ ; $K_{eq} = K_{p}$

Write this equation reverse way,

$2NH_{3}(g)$  $⇌$  $N_{2}(g) + 3H_{2}(g)$ ; $K_{eq} =$ $\frac{1}{K_{p}}$

  
    
    $2NH_{3}(g)$
    ⇌
    $N_{2}(g)$
    +
    $3H_{2}(g)$
  

  
    At t = 0
    $P^{o}$
    
    0
    
    0
  
  
    At $t = t_{eq}$
    $P_{NH3}$
    
    p
    
    3p
  

At equillibrium

$P_{$Total$} = P_{NH3} + P_{N2} + P_{H2}$

$= P_{NH3} + p + 3p$

(As $P_{NH3}  )$

$\therefore$ $P_{$Total} = 4p

$\Rightarrow$ p = $\frac{P_{total}}{4}$

Formula of

$K_{eq} =$ $\frac{p_{N2}\times \left (p_{H2}\right )^{3}}{\left (p_{NH3}\right )^{2}}$ = $\frac{1}{K_{p}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{K_{p}}$ = $\frac{p\times 27p^{3}}{\left (p_{NH3}\right )^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $(p_{NH_{3}})^{2}$ $= K_{p}$ $\times$ 27 $\times$ $\left (\frac{P_{total}}{4}\right )^{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $P_{NH3} =$ $\sqrt{K_{p}}\times (27)^{\frac{1}{2}}\times \left (\frac{P_{Total}}{4}\right )^{\frac{4}{2}}$

= $\frac{3^{\dfrac{3}{2}}K_{p}^{\dfrac{1}{2}}P_{Total}^{2}}{16}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot

text:
For the chemical reaction X $⇌$ Y,   the standard reaction Gibbs energy depends on temperature T (in K) as
$\Delta_{r}G^{o} ($in kJ mol$^{–1}) = 120$ $-\frac{3}{8}$ T. 

The major component of the reaction mixture at T is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $\mathrm{X}\mathrm{Y}$, $K=\dfrac{[\mathrm{Y}]}{[\mathrm{X}]}$ and $\Delta _{r}G^{\circ }=-RT\ln K$.

If $\Delta _{r}G^{\circ }>0$, then $K<1$ and X is the major component; if $\Delta _{r}G^{\circ }<0$, then $K>1$ and Y is the major component.

$\Delta _{r}G^{\circ }=0$ when $120-\dfrac{3}{8}T=0$, that is, at $T=320\text{K}$.

Below 320 K, $\Delta _{r}G^{\circ }>0$, so X is major at 280 K, 300 K and 315 K; above 320 K, $\Delta _{r}G^{\circ }<0$, so Y is major at 350 K. Only the pairing "X at 315 K" matches.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot

text:
Heat treatment of muscular pain involves radiation of wavelength of about 900 nm. Which spectral line of H atom is suitable for this purpose?

[$R_{H} = 1$ $\times$ $10^{5} cm^{–1}, h = 6.6$ $\times$ $10^{–34} Js, c = 3$ $\times$ $10^{8} ms^{–1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $R_{H} = 1$ $\times$ $10^{5} cm^{–1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{R_{H}}$ $= 10^{-5} cm$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{R_{H}}$ $= 10^{-7} cm$ $\times$ 100

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{R_{H}}$ = 100 nm

We know,

$\frac{1}{λ}=ν=R_{H}\times Z^{2}\left (\frac{1}{n_{L}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{H}^{2}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = $\frac{1}{R_{H}\times (1)^{2}}\times \frac{1}{\left (\frac{1}{n2L}-\frac{1}{n2H}\right )}$

[For H atom Z = 1]

$\Rightarrow$ $λ=\frac{1}{R_{H}}\times \frac{1}{\left (\frac{1}{n2L}-\frac{1}{n2H}\right )}$

$\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = $\frac{100}{\left (\frac{1}{n2L}-\frac{1}{n2H}\right )}$

Given, $λ$ = 900 nm

$\therefore$ $\frac{100}{\left (\frac{1}{n2L}-\frac{1}{n2H}\right )}$ = 900

$\Rightarrow$ $\left (\frac{1}{n_{L}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{H}^{2}}\right )=\frac{1}{9}$

By checking each options you can see

when $n_{L} = 3$ and $n_{H} =$ $\infty$ then 

$\left (\frac{1}{n_{L}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{H}^{2}}\right )=\frac{1}{9}$

$\therefore$ Option C is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot

text:
The correct match between items I and II is : 

  
    Item-I (Mixture)
    Item-II (Seperation method)
  
  
    (A)
    $H_{2}O$ : Sugar
    (P)
    Sublimation
  
  
    (B)
    $H_{2}O$ : Aniline
    (Q)
    Recrystallization
  
  
    (C)
    $H_{2}O$ : Toluene

    (R)
    Steam distillation
  
  
    
    
    (S)
    Differential extraction
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the correct match, let's understand what each separation method does :

Sublimation : The process where a substance changes directly from a solid to a gas without passing through the liquid state. This method is not applicable to any mixtures here as all components are either liquid or soluble in liquid.

Recrystallization : A method used to purify a solid. The impure compound is dissolved in a hot solvent and then allowed to slowly crystallize out as the solution cools. This could be used to separate sugar from water.

Steam Distillation : A separation process which consists in distilling water together with other volatile and non-volatile components. This could be used to separate aniline from water as aniline has a higher boiling point.

Differential extraction : It's a method that is used to separate a substance from a mixture by using an extracting solvent. This could be used to separate toluene from water as toluene is less polar and wouldn't dissolve well in water.

So, the correct match would be :

A -> Q : Water and sugar can be separated by recrystallization.

B -> R : Water and aniline can be separated by steam distillation.

C -> S : Water and toluene can be separated by differential extraction.

So, the correct option is Option B : A$\to$(Q); (B)$\to$(R); (C)$\to$(S)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot

text: The freezing point of a diluted milk sample is found to be $–0.2^{o}C$, while it should have been $–0.5^{o}C$ for pure milk. How much water has been added to pure milk to make the diluted sample?
options: 1 cup of water to 2 cups of pure milk
2 cups of water to 3 cups of pure milk
3 cups of water to 2 cups of pure milk
1 cup of water to 3 cups of pure milk
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

$\Delta T_{f} = i$ $\times$ $k_{f}$ $\times$ m

$\therefore$ $\Delta T_{$fDil. Milk} = (1) $\times$ $k_{f}$ $\times$ $m_{$dil} = 0.2  ...(1)

$\Delta T_{$fPure Milk} = (1) $\times$ $k_{f}$ $\times$ $m_{$pure} = 0.5  ...(2)

From (1) and (2), we get

$\frac{m_{pure}}{m_{dil}}=\frac{0.5}{0.2}$ = $\frac{5}{2}$ ....(3)

Assume moles of fat in both the milk samples = n

Weight of milk $= w_{1}$

and weight of water $= w_{0}$

Molality of pure milk,

$m_{$pure} = $\frac{n}{w_{1}}\times 1000$  ....(4)

Molality of diluted milk,

$m_{$dil.} = $\frac{n}{w_{1}+w_{0}}\times 1000$  ....(5)

From (4) and (5), we get

$\frac{m_{pure}}{m_{dil}}=\frac{w_{1}+w_{0}}{w_{1}}$

Using equation (3), we get

$\frac{5}{2}=\frac{w_{1}+w_{0}}{w_{1}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $5w_{1} = 2w_{1} + 2w_{0}$

$\Rightarrow$ $3w_{1} = 2w_{0}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{w_{1}}{w_{0}}=\frac{2}{3}$

Which means 3 cups of water has been added to 2 cups of pure milk.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot

text: Two blocks of the same metal having same mass and at temperature $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$, respectively, are brought in contact with each other and allowed to attain thermal equilibrium at constant pressure. The change in entropy, $\Delta$S, for this process is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When two blocks comes in contact with each other and attain thermal equilibrium then

final temperature of the blocks,

$T_{f} =$ $\frac{T_{1}+T_{2}}{2}$

$\Delta$S = $\Delta S_{1} +$ $\Delta S_{2}$

$= C_{p}$ $\ln \left (\frac{T_{f}}{T_{1}}\right )$ $+ C_{p}$ $\ln \left (\frac{T_{f}}{T_{2}}\right )$

$= C_{p}$ $\ln \left (\frac{T_{1}+T_{2}}{2T_{1}}\right )$ $+ C_{p}$ $\ln \left (\frac{T_{1}+T_{2}}{2T_{2}}\right )$

$= C_{p}$ $\ln \left (\frac{(T_{1}+T_{2})^{2}}{4T_{1}T_{2}}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 11th January Morning Slot
